1) The mutexes are never unlocked.
2) In tdr1, the mutex is first locked on "thread 1", then subsequently locked again on the main thread. The timers wake up on the main thread, not the thread that spawns the timer. This is why the re-locking fails.
3) The re-lock in tdr2 succeeds because the mutex has a behavior where re-try_lock-ing it from the same thread as has already locked it is OK. Everything except for the timer spawning happens in the main thread; only the timer spawning happens on "thread 2".

P.S.: I know that the code in the OP is just an example, but when you're on threads other than the main thread, it's *usually* better to use `OS.delay_usec()` (or `OS.delay_msec()`) than awaiting on a timer, so it's not particularly cumbersome that timers wake up on the main thread,

1 - Yes, the mutexes are never unlocked, there is no need in this case, as what is requested is that only one thread keeps returning true;

2 - That starts the oddities. Ok, the timer runs on main, but the lockins was requested before the timer in this case. At least it should run the line above it in the thread context. Why would the timer make the locking context change from the thread requested to the main thread?

3 - what is being pointed is that the code is being run in a split manner, part of it in the evoked thread, and part on the main one. Now thats certantly because of the timer. Is that because it is a SceneTreeTimer? If it was just a new instance of Timer it would need to be added to the tree, and sincronization would be needed as well?

4 - Now this is a behaviour that is not very acurate, at least i cant use OS.delays on my project in that part because it seens to not work. Maybe its another thing i need to report. The case is that this threads manage individual network peers, and if i frame-limit using OS.delay, - i supose- something on the packet-pushing low-level aspect gets frozen as well, and the network transmission seens to not work when the thread is in the delay state. Awaiting timers does not create the internal freeze, and the conection remain stable, even if the frame-pushing is artificialy throtled, the frame-transmission keeps running bethen the freezes.
